correction.text: Strongest feature: Craig exposes a concrete diachronic consequence: if infinite elapsed time and correspondence independently suffice for completion, the countdown should have ended yesterday and at every earlier stage, making the present terminus explanatorily arbitrary. Principal limitation: This reasoning assumes the disputed, temporally unindexed sufficiency principle, while ordered countdown labels may determine that zero occurs only now; infinitely many predecessors therefore do not themselves establish earlier completion. Live burden: Craig must show that duration and correspondence determine completion independently of the indexed schedule, or expose an internal contradiction in Malpass's tense-sensitive account, instead of reiterating the contested assumption. Locked score: 79 recognizes an exceptionally relevant, vividly intelligible diagnostic with explicit conditional structure and direct burden contact, while discounting its insufficiently defended warrant, overstated necessity, and incomplete engagement with the strongest schedule-based alternative.
